Sampled HR/NDCG can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; larger samples reduce neither every bias nor exposure confounding. Both uniform and popularity-based negatives can disagree with full-catalog rankings in sequential recommendation. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [Dallmann et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045). A 2025 study separates sampling reliability into model separability, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and alignment with true preferences—useful diagnostic dimensions, without treating full-catalog logged-data ranking as unbiased ground truth. [Pereira et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398).

Suggested application: retain the pinned validation evaluator and selection objective. Build separate chronological prefix probes exclusively from public training histories; exclude the target and subsequent interactions from each input. Unless probe targets were withheld from optimization, describe results as training diagnostics, not generalization estimates. Compare HR@10, NDCG@10 and target rank using fixed unique sampled negatives, several candidate sizes, and full-catalog ranking on a manageable user subset. Stratify by training-only target popularity and history length; report group counts. Use paired user-cluster bootstrap intervals for changes, resampling within category before computing the four-category macro average. These are proposed procedures, not demonstrated findings for this benchmark.

Validate probes before using them to change training: inject increasing score noise or deliberately demote targets and require worsening ranking metrics. Separately shuffle histories, remove recent events, and replace histories across users to test sequence dependence. Shuffling has research precedent, but weak degradation can reflect weak sequential structure rather than a broken probe. [Klenitskiy et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008). Keep these inference-only perturbations separate from deployed predictions; retain one NextItNet checkpoint per category.
